plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. Since I win only when I have the highest bid and pay the second-highest bid, bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever it's profitable (value > second-highest bid) and never overpay. This eliminates strategic risk from guessing others' bids and maximizes expected profit.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction) with independent private values. In such auctions, bidding truthfully (bidding exactly my value) is a dominant strategy, regardless of what other bidders do. This maximizes expected profit because I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid, and I only pay that second-highest bid, ensuring I never pay more than my value and always capture positive surplus when I win. I will bid my true value of $15.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' actions. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With a value of $10, I should bid exactly $10 to ensure I only win when it's profitable and pay a fair price when I do.
